node: K-12 virtual schooling and alternative digital schooling platforms
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the direct-public-company universe for the K-12 virtual schooling node. The clearest reference leaders are Stride and Pearson because both operate or support full-time online K-12 school programs. The underfollowed discovery lane is thinner: Nerdy is a small/micro-cap online tutoring and school-platform vendor with district exposure but weaker evidence as a full virtual-school operator; RCM Technologies is a speculative second-order staffing and telepractice supplier for school districts, relevant to the special-education and compliance burden inside virtual/hybrid schooling. This pass avoids unrelated higher-ed and workforce-training names unless they directly touch K-12 virtual or district services. Layer 1B expands the public-company universe around the scarce operating inputs for compliant K-12 virtual schooling: full-stack online public-school operators, virtual-school curriculum/platform vendors, SIS/LMS/attendance/administrative software, and regulated special-education or teletherapy staffing. The list intentionally uses Stride and Pearson as reference anchors, then adds underfollowed infrastructure and regulated-service suppliers that could matter if virtual or alternative digital schooling scales. Layer 1B expansion for the K-12 virtual schooling node found one obvious public reference leader and three less-obvious public-market exposures: teacher/staffing supply, supplemental digital curriculum, and district tutoring/intervention.
